clue.text: Painted in water-colours, not by Landseer?

definitions.text: Painted in water-colours, not by Landseer?

parts.words: Painted in water-colours, not by Landseer?
parts.note: Landseer split as land-seer: a picture of the ocean rather than of land, painted in the waters' colours

explanation.surface: A gallery note that a watercolour is not the work of the Victorian animal painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Edwin Landseer was a Victorian painter famed for animals such as the Trafalgar Square lions; the joke reads his name as 'land seer', so the picture shows the waves instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A marine view is a painting of the ocean, the counterpart of a landscape.

clue.text: Equestrian ability possessed by large majority

definitions.meaning: a rider's firm, secure position in the saddle
a parliamentary constituency held by a big margin

explanation.definitionFit: A rider's secure posture in the saddle, and an election constituency that cannot realistically be lost.

clue.text: Queen expelling one Roman from place in Egypt

indicators.note: expelling says a letter is thrown out of the place name

parts.note: Alexandria is the Egyptian port city
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A queen drives an Italian out of an Egyptian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One Roman' suggests a citizen of Rome; it is the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen consort of Edward VII of Britain.

clue.text: Beg for keys

parts.note: C is a musical key
A is a musical key
D is a musical key
G is a musical key
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Pleading to be given a set of keys.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrounge or ask for something free.

clue.text: Philosopher acting for company, partly

parts.note: Plato, the Greek philosopher
an actor on stage is on

explanation.surface: A philosopher partly playing a role in a theatre company.
explanation.definitionFit: A military unit forming one subdivision of an infantry company.

clue.text: Light shoe right for inferior racehorse

parts.note: a plate is a light horseshoe used for racing

explanation.surface: A farrier fits a lightweight shoe to a horse of little ability.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing slang a low-class horse that runs in cheap plate races is so called.

clue.text: Businessmen folding trousers with damaged legs?

parts.note: lame means hobbled by injured legs
ducks are trousers of strong white cloth

explanation.surface: Men in business clothes folding their trousers, though with injured legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Folding' looks like creasing trousers but means failing, as a business folds.
explanation.definitionFit: Failing firms or people needing help, an idiom from the stock exchange for defaulters.

clue.text: In river, second bait finally is attracting bites

indicators.note: In says the following letters go into the river

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word bait

explanation.surface: An angler on a river finds his bait at last draws fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetising food tempts you to eat; delicious enough to be bitten.

clue.text: Is, like boxer, coming out of retirement

indicators.note: like a boxer means in the place a boxer is, so the word Is goes into his arena

parts.note: a boxer fights in the ring

explanation.surface: A former boxer is making his comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: Retirement here means going to bed, so coming out of it is getting up.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting out of bed in the morning, retirement being bedtime.

clue.text: A couple of chaps supposed to help Leo

parts.note: Jack is a man's name
Al is a man's name

explanation.surface: Two men meant to assist a fellow called Leo.
explanation.walkthrough: Leo is the lion; the scavenging animal was traditionally thought to hunt prey for it, the so-called lion's provider.
explanation.definitionFit: Folklore made this wild dog the lion's provider, finding food for the big cat.

clue.text: Place for arms runners

definitions.meaning: in heraldry the background of a shield on which the arms are displayed
all the competitors taking part in a race, especially horses

explanation.definitionFit: Heraldry's name for a shield's background, and racing's word for all the starters together.

clue.text: Mass trial arranged for flappers

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of these two words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A big court case is set up to deal with some agitated people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flappers' suggests 1920s young women, but here it means people in a flap, panicking.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in a flap is a panicker who spreads needless fear.

clue.text: Labour activity at grass-roots level?

parts.note: reads like local party politics, but means the literal work of digging into the soil where grass roots grow

explanation.surface: Local Labour Party campaigners doing the groundwork in the constituencies.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard preliminary groundwork, literally the labour of digging with a garden tool.

clue.text: The same urge to be senior member

parts.note: do is short for ditto, meaning the same
a yen is a longing or urge

explanation.surface: Wanting exactly what everyone wants is the way to become the eldest of the group.
explanation.definitionFit: The most respected or longest-serving person in a body is its dean.

clue.text: Writer tells how to get Yorktown loser from Cornwall

parts.note: the instruction begins with the verb for appending letters to a word

indicators.note: from says the county's name is taken away from the general's, leaving the two letters to be appended

parts.note: Lord Cornwallis, the British general who surrendered at Yorktown in 1781
the English county, written as it is
the instruction ends with the adverb saying the letters go on the end

explanation.surface: An author explains how the British general who lost Yorktown came from Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer split up is an instruction: append the two letters by which the general's name exceeds the county's, and the county becomes the general. Cornwallis lost to Washington at Yorktown, ending the American war.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Addison was an English essayist, co-founder of The Spectator.

clue.text: Rack to put case on

definitions.meaning: something that stretches, as a torture rack or a frame for canvas
a carried bed for a patient, a medical case

explanation.definitionFit: A frame that pulls taut, and the litter on which an injured patient is carried.

clue.text: Key operator holds things for us

definitions.meaning: one who fastens something with a key
a small cupboard where belongings are stored, as at a gym or school

explanation.definitionFit: One who secures with a key, and a lockable storage cupboard.

clue.text: One involved with cost and no end of money

definitions.text: One involved with cost and no end of money

indicators.note: involved means the letters are tangled together into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: no end of says the last letter of money is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone concerned with costs and with vast amounts of money.
explanation.walkthrough: I with COST and MONE (money without its Y) is anagrammed as signalled by 'involved'; read whole, the clue describes such an expert.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert in finance and the production of wealth deals with costs and money.

clue.text: Head's short cut for annual production of scholars?

definitions.meaning: a short boyish hairstyle popular with women in the 1920s
the yearly harvest of pupils from the famous English public school

explanation.definitionFit: A cropped 1920s haircut, and whimsically the yearly yield of boys leaving the public school near Windsor.

clue.text: Boatman in Hebrides

definitions.meaning: one of the three men in Jerome K. Jerome's Three Men in a Boat
an island area of the Outer Hebrides, joined to Lewis

explanation.definitionFit: A companion in Jerome's comic boating novel, and a part of the Outer Hebrides famous for its tweed.

clue.text: How to train porpoises, for example

definitions.meaning: a group of sea mammals or fish swimming together

explanation.definitionFit: A verb for teaching, and the collective noun for a pod of porpoises or a shoal of fish.

clue.text: Complete training, as three quarters may do

definitions.meaning: to finish a course, especially at a military academy, with a parade
in rugby the three-quarter backs throw the ball wide to each other

explanation.definitionFit: Graduating from military training, and the rugby move of throwing the ball wide along the back line.

clue.text: Losing one's tan a little time afterwards in Sicily?

indicators.note: afterwards puts the little time after the first piece

parts.note: a fading tan leaves the skin paler
mo is short for moment

explanation.surface: Back from a Sicilian holiday, the tan fades soon after.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Sicily, so a place found on that island.

clue.text: Legislation upset crank found in cabinet

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: law means legislation
a nut is an eccentric or crank

explanation.surface: A government cabinet contains a madman who has overturned the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet' suggests ministers, but it is furniture, often veneered in this wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine hardwood widely used for veneering furniture.

clue.text: Among most, doctors removed anxiety

indicators.note: removed says the doctors are taken out of the words before

parts.note: MO stands for medical officer, a doctor; two of them give MO twice

explanation.surface: Most people feel uneasy once their doctors have been taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: A German loan word for deep dread or existential unease.

clue.text: Children's author wants decoration round edge

indicators.note: round says the medal letters go around the edge

parts.note: GM is the George Medal, a British gallantry award
rim means edge

explanation.surface: A writer for children wants a decorative border.
explanation.definitionFit: The brothers Jacob and Wilhelm collected German fairy tales for young readers.

clue.text: Biggest D-day casualty

parts.note: D-day here is Decimal Day, February 1971, when Britain's old coins began to go; the largest coin was already withdrawn

explanation.surface: Sounds like the greatest loss of life in the Normandy landings of 1944.
explanation.walkthrough: D-day suggests 1944, but it is Britain's Decimal Day; the half-crown, worth two shillings and sixpence, was the largest pre-decimal coin and was withdrawn in 1970 ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: An old British silver coin worth an eighth of a pound, demonetised before decimalisation.

clue.text: Challenge for some athletic Aberdonian?

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A test of strength for a sporty man from Aberdeen.
explanation.walkthrough: Tossing the heavy pole is a test of strength at Scottish Highland games.
explanation.definitionFit: The long tree trunk tossed at Highland games is a test of strength.

clue.text: Next man's constructed from rib — enough, is it?

indicators.note: constructed from says these letters are built into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Was the man beside Adam made from a rib, and is that sufficient?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Eve being made from Adam's rib; 'enough, is it?' wonders whether a rib suffices.
explanation.definitionFit: The person living next door or nearby.

clue.text: 19's Rabbit, including one born in this patch

indicators.note: including means the first piece holds the next inside it

parts.note: 19 across is the surname of Joel Chandler Harris, whose Uncle Remus stories feature Brer Rabbit
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The rabbit of the Uncle Remus tales, with one born in this very patch.
explanation.walkthrough: Brer Rabbit boasts he was born and bred in the prickly patch where Brer Fox throws him to escape.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorny wild rose or bramble, the plant making up the thicket of the story.

clue.text: Sound quality of British seen in great physician

indicators.note: seen in says the abbreviation sits inside the other word

parts.note: from the proverb 'Time is the great physician', as it heals all

explanation.surface: A British doctor of renown judged on the tone of his voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great physician' invites a famous doctor such as Galen, but it is the proverb that time heals.
explanation.definitionFit: The distinctive tone colour of a voice or instrument.

clue.text: It raises the standing of bell-ringers

definitions.text: It raises the standing of bell-ringers

parts.words: It raises the standing of bell-ringers
parts.note: not church campanologists but callers who press the doorbell and stand on the raised slab outside

explanation.surface: Something that boosts the reputation of church change-ringers.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised step at the front entrance, where visitors stand waiting.
